notes.headline: HP grows revenue 9% as AI PCs reach almost 60% of shipments, and the stock jumps 11.5% despite a cautious outlook
notes.takeaway: Fourth-quarter revenue rose 9.3% to $16.0 billion, but adjusted EPS fell 10.8% to $0.83 as memory costs squeezed PC margins. HP guided fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of $3.15–3.45, raised its dividend to $0.31 and the shares rose 11.5%.
results: Fourth-quarter revenue was $16.0 billion, up 9.3%. Personal Systems revenue rose 14% to $11.8 billion, with commercial PCs up 23% and consumer PCs down 7%, while units fell 29%; the gap between revenue and units reflects much higher selling prices as memory and storage costs were passed on. The Personal Systems operating margin was only 3.0%. Printing revenue slipped 1% to $4.3 billion at a 19.7% margin.

GAAP EPS was flat at $0.84 and adjusted EPS fell 10.8% to $0.83, both including a benefit from tariff refunds. For the full fiscal year, revenue rose 9.5% to $60.5 billion, adjusted EPS rose 6.7% to $3.33 and free cash flow was $3.3 billion, of which $2.3 billion went back to shareholders.
mgmt: Interim chief executive Bruce Broussard said AI PCs reached nearly 60% of shipments and that HP is taking steps to address memory and storage cost pressures. He expects new on-device AI capabilities to drive several waves of device replacement.

Chief financial officer Karen Parkhill described the fiscal 2027 outlook as a prudent view of continued cost and demand pressures. HP expects first-quarter adjusted EPS of $0.66 to $0.76, full-year adjusted EPS of $3.15 to $3.45 and free cash flow of $2.9 to $3.1 billion. From next year stock compensation is excluded from adjusted figures, which flatters the comparison.
view: The numbers themselves were weak. Units down almost 30%, a 3% margin in PCs and lower adjusted earnings in the quarter show how hard the surge in memory prices has hit hardware makers. Revenue growth came from price, not volume, and the full-year guidance midpoint is roughly flat with this year even after the change in how stock compensation is treated, so underlying earnings are expected to decline.

The 11.5% rise to $31.15 reflects how low expectations were. Before the report the shares traded at around 8 to 9 times this year’s adjusted earnings and analysts on average had a target below the share price. A guidance range that did not collapse, a higher dividend and $3 billion of expected free cash flow were enough to trigger a relief rally in an unloved stock.

At about 9.5 times next year’s EPS midpoint and a dividend yield near 4%, HP is a cash-return story with a cyclical overlay. The upside case is a commercial PC refresh as Windows and AI hardware requirements change while memory costs ease; the downside is that the company runs out of pricing power before costs normalise and the dividend absorbs most of the cash flow. A new permanent chief executive is also still to be named.
notes.watch: Memory and storage prices through 2027, the Personal Systems margin returning toward its 5–7% target range, the appointment of a permanent chief executive, and first-quarter EPS against the $0.66–0.76 range.
